mcq.q: In compliance work, a control is…
options: A report that is written once a year
A concrete measure the system or team carries out
The name of the lawyer responsible for it
The text of the law that applies to it
mcq.why: Controls make obligations real: approvals, logs, tests.

mcq.q: Which is the best evidence that human oversight works?
options: A screenshot from last year’s audit
A promise in the product brief
Approval records produced on every decision
A slide saying people review decisions
mcq.why: Records produced continuously by the system prove the control ran.

mcq.q: Evidence is dated 250 days ago and the freshness rule is 180 days. The row is…
options: Fine, since the control exists
Deleted from the matrix
Fine for another 70 days
Stale and needs new evidence
mcq.why: 250 > 180, so the evidence no longer counts.

mcq.q: An obligation has no control in the matrix. This is…
options: Covered by the general policy
A gap that needs an owner and a control
A documentation formatting error
Acceptable if no incident happened
mcq.why: Gaps are the real compliance risk.

mcq.q: 50 evidence rows refreshed by hand twice a year at 1 hour each take…
options: 200 hours a year
25 hours a year
100 hours a year
50 hours a year

mcq.q: Who should interpret what an obligation means for your system?
options: Engineering together with legal and compliance
The model provider’s sales team
Whoever writes the release notes
Engineering alone, from the law’s text
mcq.why: Interpretation is a legal judgement applied to a technical design.

mcq.q: A new feature ships but its obligations are not added to the matrix. The likely result is…
options: Automatic coverage by old controls
A smaller attack surface
Faster releases with no downside
Controls and evidence missing at audit
mcq.why: Features bring obligations; the matrix must grow with them.

mcq.q: 40 of 50 rows get evidence from the pipeline automatically; the rest take 2 hours a year each. Manual work is…
options: 80 hours a year
100 hours a year
40 hours a year
20 hours a year

mcq.q: Why prefer evidence produced by the pipeline?
options: It is current and does not depend on memory
Auditors refuse documents written by people
It removes the need for owners
It is always shorter to read
mcq.why: Automatic evidence stays fresh and complete.

mcq.q: A kill-switch exists but was never tested. For the control matrix this means…
options: No evidence the control works yet
The control is proven by existing
The obligation is met in full
Testing would break production
mcq.why: Untested controls lack evidence; run a drill.
distractors: Drills are designed to be safe.

mcq.q: In a risk-based AI law, duties depend mainly on…
options: The model’s parameter count
The number of users only
The use’s risk tier and your role
The programming language used
mcq.why: Tier and role (provider or deployer) decide duties.

mcq.q: A company buys a CV screening tool and uses it on applicants. It is mainly…
options: Outside any AI duties
A deployer of a high-risk system
A provider of a minimal-risk system
A provider of a general-purpose model
mcq.why: Using it under its own authority makes it a deployer; employment is high risk.

mcq.q: A customer support chatbot typically carries which duty?
options: A full conformity assessment by a notified body
No duties of any kind at all
Telling people they are interacting with AI
A ban on deploying it anywhere
mcq.why: Transparency duties apply to systems that interact with people.
distractors: That is for some high-risk systems.

mcq.q: An inventory of 30 uses has 3 high-risk systems at 10 controls each and 9 transparency systems at 2. Matrix rows needed:
Why record minimal-risk uses in the inventory too?
options: Because they carry the same duties
Because regulators ban them
To increase the size of the inventory
So the classification itself can be checked
mcq.why: Auditors check how each use was classified.

mcq.q: A system is minimal risk under the AI law but processes personal data. Which statement is right?
options: Privacy law is replaced by AI law
Privacy law can still apply in full
No law applies to it at all
It becomes high risk automatically
mcq.why: Laws overlap; privacy duties apply regardless of AI tier.

mcq.q: A bank’s loan pre-qualification model is most likely…
options: Minimal risk, since it only pre-qualifies
Outside scope, since staff make the final call
High risk, since it affects access to credit
Prohibited, since it uses personal data
mcq.why: Credit scoring is a typical high-risk area.
distractors: Staff review does not remove the tier.

mcq.q: Obligations under the EU AI Act apply…
options: All at once from the day it passed
Only to companies based in the EU
Only to general-purpose models
In phases from 2025, with dates to check
mcq.why: Application is phased, and amendments to dates have been proposed.
distractors: It can apply to non-EU providers and deployers serving the EU.

mcq.q: If 1 use of 30 must be redesigned, 3 are high risk, 9 have transparency duties, how many are minimal risk?
Your company builds an AI agent on a hosted model and offers it to customers. For that agent, you are…
options: Neither, since the model provider is responsible
Its provider, while using a model from another
A notified body for the model
Only a deployer, since the model is not yours
mcq.why: Building and offering a system makes you its provider.

mcq.q: Why are deletion requests harder in LLM systems than in plain databases?
options: Deletion is forbidden in AI systems
LLMs cannot read personal data at all
Personal data is copied into many derived stores
Databases cannot delete records
mcq.why: Chunks, vectors, caches, memories, logs and datasets all hold copies.

mcq.q: Deleting only the 3 source records of 67 copies removes about…
A person asks for deletion, but the bank must keep transaction records by law. The right response is…
options: Ignore the request until the next audit
Delete everything, including the legal records
Delete what can be deleted and explain what is kept
Refuse the whole request with no explanation
mcq.why: Retained data needs a documented legal reason.

mcq.q: Which design most reduces the work of future deletion requests?
options: Storing all chats forever for later training
Keeping personal data out of prompts and logs
Using one large shared index for everything
Copying the data into every available cache
mcq.why: Minimisation means fewer copies to find.

mcq.q: Deleting training rows does what to a model already trained on them?
options: Removes them from the weights at once
Nothing; the model may still reflect them
Makes the model refuse those topics
Forces the model to retrain itself
mcq.why: Models must be flagged for review or retraining (13.6).

mcq.q: Before acting on an access request, you must…
options: Delete their data first
Wait for a second request
Verify the requester’s identity
Ask why they want it
mcq.why: Handing data to the wrong person is a breach.

mcq.q: Traces are kept 30 days and the response deadline is one month. Should you wait for traces to expire?
options: Yes; expiry will handle it automatically
Yes; traces never count as personal data
No; traces must legally be kept forever
No; delete or redact them as part of the request
mcq.why: Relying on timing is fragile; act on every store.
distractors: Risky if retention changes or overlaps the deadline.

mcq.q: A system makes solely automated decisions with significant effects. Privacy law often requires…
options: A larger model for such decisions
Encrypting the model weights
Meaningful human review and an explanation
Hiding the decision logic entirely
mcq.why: Rights around automated decisions include human involvement.

mcq.q: A store finds 400 trace copies for one heavy shopper versus 12 elsewhere. The best fix is…
options: Delete and rebuild the vector index every week
Stop answering questions from heavy shoppers
Keep the traces for longer, to be safe
Redact personal data before traces are written
mcq.why: Redaction at write time removes the bulk of copies.

mcq.q: Embeddings of a person’s text are…
options: Personal data to include in deletion
Exempt from privacy rules
Only kept in memory, never stored
Anonymous because they are numbers
mcq.why: Embeddings can leak their source (16.5) and are derived personal data.

interview.followUp: How do you design around it?

interview.q: A deletion request arrives for data that legal duties require you to keep. What do you do?
How would you reduce the number of stores personal data reaches?
How do you prove a deletion was complete?

interview.q: Design privacy into a new assistant that handles customer data.
interview.followUp: What do you decide before the first prompt is written?

interview.q: Plan how training and evaluation sets stay compliant over time.

mcq.q: Which is a basic transparency duty for a chatbot?
options: Showing its weights to every user
Publishing its training data in full
Explaining every token it predicts
Telling people they are talking to an AI
mcq.why: Disclosure of AI interaction is the common baseline.

mcq.q: Machine-readable labels on generated media are often implemented with…
options: A longer and more descriptive file name
Content credentials such as C2PA metadata
A larger font in the visible caption
A different image format for every file
mcq.why: Provenance metadata travels with the file.

mcq.q: Each of 8 fields goes missing 2% of the time. The share of complete records is about…
mcq.why: 0.98 multiplied 8 times ≈ 0.85.

mcq.q: Why must decision records include model and prompt versions?
options: To make each record longer and fuller
Because users often ask to see them
To reproduce and explain past outputs
To reduce the cost of storing records
mcq.why: Versions let you rebuild what happened (18.1).

mcq.q: Decision records are stored in a table staff can edit. The main risk is…
options: Records take more space
Queries become slower
Labels disappear from content
The audit trail can be changed
mcq.why: Records must be append-only to be trusted.

mcq.q: A voice assistant greets callers naturally and never says it is an AI. What is missing?
options: Disclosure at the start of the call
A higher-quality, more natural voice
A shorter and simpler greeting
A different underlying language model
mcq.why: Voice needs spoken disclosure; there is no banner.

mcq.q: 1 million decision records a year at 2 KB each need about…
options: 20 GB a year
2 TB a year
200 MB a year
2 GB a year

mcq.q: Which check catches missing fields in decision records early?
options: A completeness check that alerts in the pipeline
Reading the records by hand every month
A yearly audit of a sample of records
Asking users to report any gaps they see
mcq.why: Automatic checks find gaps on the first bad record.

mcq.q: A label appears on the website but not in the mobile app. This is…
options: Fine if the website is labelled
A design choice with no impact
A gap in one channel to fix
Required only for print media
mcq.why: Every channel where content appears needs the label.
distractors: Users in the app are not told.

mcq.q: Why must audit samples be drawn at random?
options: A chosen sample can hide problems
Auditors cannot read selected cases
Random samples need no checking
Random samples are always larger
mcq.why: Selection lets problems be steered away from review.

mcq.q: How many clean random checks support "below 5% breaches" with 95% confidence?
mcq.why: The smallest n where 0.95 to the power n falls below 0.05 is 59.

mcq.q: 20 clean checks support a breach rate below about…
4 breaches in 60 checks is 6.7% with an interval of 2.6% to 15.9%. Is a 5% target met?
options: Yes, since the lower end is below 5%
No, the rate is certainly above 5%
Not shown either way; sample more
Yes, since 6.7% is close to 5%
mcq.why: The interval straddles 5%; the evidence is inconclusive.
distractors: The lower end is not the estimate.

mcq.q: ISO/IEC 42001 is…
options: A law that bans every high-risk AI system
A benchmark of model accuracy on many tasks
A file format for storing model weights
A certifiable AI management system standard
mcq.why: It audits the management system around AI.
distractors: It is a standard, not a law.

mcq.q: Errors cluster on disruption days. A sound audit design is…
options: Sample disruption and normal periods separately
Sample only the quiet days, for speed
Average all the days into one single sample
Skip audits entirely during disruptions
mcq.why: Stratifying by period shows where breaches concentrate.

mcq.q: Checking 299 decisions at 5 minutes each takes about…
options: 25 hours
15 hours
2.5 hours
50 hours
mcq.why: 299 × 5 = 1,495 minutes ≈ 25 hours.

mcq.q: The NIST AI RMF is best described as…
options: A mandatory regulation of the European Union
A voluntary framework for managing AI risk
A body that certifies AI management systems
An open-source model released by NIST
mcq.why: It structures risk work: govern, map, measure, manage.
distractors: It is from the US and voluntary.

mcq.q: An audit finding has no owner or due date. The likely outcome is…
options: It stays open until the next audit
It is removed from the report
The auditor closes it automatically
It fixes itself over time
mcq.why: Findings need owners and dates to be closed.

mcq.q: Which result statement is most honest?
options: A few breaches were found, which is about the usual
0 breaches in 59 checks: below 5% with 95% confidence
The checks all looked fine overall this quarter
0 breaches in 20 checks, so there are no problems
mcq.why: It states the sample and what it supports.
